fatal_errors: The hypothesis addresses hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10 rather than the target Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W design space and Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 alloy.
It replaces the target composition-screening method based on rule-of-mixtures modulus, VEC, and density with an unvalidated microstructure-aware machine-learning surrogate.
It specifies tensile and fracture-toughness testing, whereas the demonstrated target result was room-temperature quasi-static compression of an as-cast alloy.
The claimed 20% error reduction, ±15% toughness accuracy, and tenfold efficiency gain are not supported by the cited evidence.
The proposed benchmark is not blinded and does not directly compare against the target equimolar NbMoTaVW baseline or the relevant competing prediction methods.
explanation: The response follows the misleading HfNbTiVAl10 premise rather than reconstructing the target study. The target intervention screened 38,326 Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W compositions using average iso-strain/iso-stress rule-of-mixtures modulus, VEC, and density, selected Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5, and validated it experimentally in room-temperature compression. Its central mechanism was reduced VEC lowering the Peierls–Nabarro barrier and promoting dislocation slip, yielding 35.7% compressive fracture strain while retaining 1115 MPa yield strength. None of these defining elements, baselines, conditions, or outcomes is recovered. The proposed hybrid surrogate is scientifically conceivable and its domain-of-applicability caveat is reasonable, but the cited papers only support physics-informed ML and integrated computational screening in broad terms; they do not validate microstructure-conditioned toughness prediction or the numerical gains asserted. The falsification design also lacks prospective blinding, held-out processing conditions, predefined specimen counts, and a stringent comparison against incumbent models, while indentation-based methods would not necessarily provide valid fracture toughness.
